word_order: SVO | Subjects precede verbs which precede objects in the examples (e.g. “Blood goes away from the heart” = Blood (S) goes (V) away from the heart (O)).
register: written, expository/encyclopedic prose (formal factual descriptions, historical notes and instructions rather than spontaneous conversational speech).
non_boundary_traps: often introduces an appositive (e.g. "called ziggurats") not a clause break
lists or enumerations introduced by "such as" or "including"
unstable_prefix_signals: infinitival marker often followed by verb phrase that changes attachment
notes_for_prompt_writer: This source is formal written English; prefer conservative segmentation that preserves noun+relative/subordinate attachments. Delay emitting a segment when you encounter complementizers or relative pronouns (which/who/that) or subordinators (because/although/if/when/as) since what follows will typically attach to a previous noun or clause. Avoid splitting at commas that enclose appositives, parentheticals or date/number commas, and treat enumerations introduced by "such as/including" as internal to the prior phrase unless a full independent clause begins.
